contexts.text: Wash ye your feet () = that (the Divine) should put on something natural, in order that in the state in which He then was, the Lord might the better perceive. Explained. AC 2162:12.
Wash ye your feet () = application to the Natural of it.
Water to wash his feet () = purification there. Explained.
(On the washing of feet. See Foot, and at AC 3148. AC 5669.)

These things were signified by the washings in the Ancient Church; and the same were represented in the Jewish Church... The (former) did not believe that they were purified by the washing, but by the washing off of the unclean things of the natural man... But (the latter) believed that they were purified by the washing.
That washing = the washing off of these uncleannesses. Illustrated.

(Thus it is evident) that to wash one's self involves something special and peculiar, namely, spiritual washing; that is, purification from the uncleannesses which cleave to man inwardly; and therefore they who knew this, and thought about the purification of the heart - that is, the removal from the natural man of the evils of the love of self and of the love of the world these observed the rite of washing merely as an act of external worship which was to be done because it was commanded; whereas they who did not know this... worshipped this rite in an idolatrous manner. Explained.

Good and angelic Spirits, who fall into a state of the love of self and from that into a state of falsity, are remitted a little into their natural... state, and are there imbued with Knowledges... which apply to that condition of things. This is signified by to wash with water in the evening (; ).
Thou wilt wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow () = to be purified from sins by the reception and putting on of the Lord's righteousness.
Naaman's washing in Jordan represented baptism. Explained.
Sanctification was represented by the ritual of washing and of cleansing. Illustrated.
He washed his faces () = he disposed so that it should not appear. Explained.
(Thus) purification, which was represented by the washing of the garments, is effected by means of the truths of faith.
He washes his clothing in wine () = that His Natural is the Divine truth from His Divine good: for to wash = to purify.

To wash at the river () = worship from what is false; for to wash = purification from uncleannesses as spiritually understood; and therefore it = worship; because worship is for the sake of purification.
To wash = to purify.
The washing of the feet = purification from sins, which is effected by means of the truths of faith; for by these man is taught how he should live.
On this account (the inhabitants of Jupiter) wash and cleanse their faces very much.
Let them wash their garments () = the purification of truths; for to wash = purification from spiritual uncleannesses.
The washing of the hands over the heifer at a rapid river () = purification from this evil, because it had been done from the immoderate zeal of one who is ignorant of truth. AC 9262:3.
Man is regenerated by means of the truths of faith, and this was signified by the washings by which, in ancient times, they were cleansed; and the same is now signified by the waters of baptism.
Washing = the purification of the internal man.
By (Aaron's) washing of his flesh () is signified that the purification (of good) is effected by means of the truths which are from good.
All the expiation which was effected by means of washings, burnt-offerings, and sacrifices, represented the purification of the heart from evils and falsities, thus regeneration...
Thou shalt wash them with waters () = purification by means of the truths of faith. AC 10243. Signified, Explained.
Washed = purified and regenerated.

Thou shalt wash the intestines () = the purification of the lowest things... The purification which was represented by the washing, is purification from evils and falsities; for these are uncleannesses in the spiritual sense. AC 10235. AC 10237, Signified.
To wash the thighs () = the purification of the natural man.
Aaron and his sons shall wash out of it away () = a representative of the purification and regeneration of man by the Lord. Explained. AC 10240. Explained.
(The washing of the disciples' feet by the Lord () Fully explained.)

To wash the head, hands, and feet = regeneration; and so also does he that is washed. Thus to wash the feet = to purify the Natural of man; for unless this is purified and cleansed with a man while he lives in the world, it can never be purified afterwards. Explained.

That he who has been regenerated is not to be purified except as to the Natural, is meant by, he that is washed needeth not to be washed except as to the feet, and is clean every whit. And that all purification is effected by the Lord alone, is meant by,If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with Me.
For the washing of baptism is nothing but spiritual washing, which is regeneration. LJ 18:4.
General article.
(References to passages on the subject of washing.)
That a total washing... by immersion in the waters of Jordan, = regeneration itself, the same as baptism. References.

By the washing (of the disciples' feet) is meant spiritual washing, which is purification from evils. To wash the head and the hands = to purify the internal man; and to wash the feet = to purify the external man. That when the internal man has been purified, the external man is to be purified, is meant by, he that is washed needeth not to be washed except as to the feet. That all purification from evils is done by the Lord alone, is meant by, If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with Me.
Among the Jews, washing represented purification from evils; and this is what is signified by washing, in the Word...

That loveth us, and washeth us from our sins in His own blood () = who, from love and mercy, reforms and regenerates men by means of His Divine truths from the Word. It is evident that to wash us from sins = to purify from evils, and thus to reform and regenerate; for regeneration is a spiritual washing. AE 30.

And have washed their robes () = who have cleansed the things of their religion from the evils of falsity. To wash, in the Word, = to cleanse one's self from evils and falsities. ( = the removal of falsities by means of temptations. AE 475.)
The washings which were commanded to the Israelites. Explained. TCR 671, Illustrated.
The Lord retained... baptism instead of the washings.
That the washing of the spirit of man was meant by the washing of his body. Illustrated.
(Thus) washings, and baptizings also, (are useless) unless the internal of the man be purified from evils and falsities. Explained.

The Lord conjoins good with truth in the spiritual mind... and this comes to man's perception only obscurely; but it becomes more and more manifest as the man studies the good of life, which is done in the natural man. This is what is meant by... he that has once been washed, needeth not to be washed except as to the feet; for in proportion as a man does goods, a conjunction is effected of spiritual good with natural, and this is done by means of a moral life... and this is done as often as the man thinks and wills what is good as of himself.
The washings (among the Israelites) merely represented purifications from evils and falsities by means of the truths of faith and a life according to them. References. AE 275:22.

Wash thyself in the pool of Siloam... He went and washed himself, and came seeing ()... The pool of Siloam = the Word in the letter; and to be washed there = to be purified from falsities and evils. AE 475:17.
I washed thee () = to purify from evils. AE 329:24. AE 375:27. Explained. AE 475:8.
That to wash = to purify from evils and falsities. References.
I wash my hands in innocence () = to be purified from evils and falsities.

In ancient times... washings represented purifications from falsities and evils; for the reason that waters = truths, and uncleannesses, falsities and evils; and all purification from falsities and evils is effected by means of truths. This was why washings were instituted by command among the sons of Israel... Illustrated.
To wash the hands and feet () = to purify the natural man; and to wash the flesh () = to purify the spiritual man.
He that is washed () = one who is interiorly clean; needeth not save to wash his feet = that then he is to be cleansed exteriorly. AE 666:2, Explained.

That to wash = to purify from falsities and evils, is evident from, Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before Mine eyes; cease to do evil ()... Wash thine heart from wickedness, Jerusalem, that thou mayest be saved ()... Wash me from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin... (). Explained.
to wash the hands in innocency () = to bear witness that one is innocent, and pure from evils and falsities; for the washing of the hands was a testification of innocence. Illustrated.
Naaman washing in the waters of Jordan seven times () = complete purification from falsified truths (by means of introductory truths). AE 724:8.
The washing of the disciples' feet, represented purification from evils and falsities by the Lord by means of the Divine truth.
